# 8-Week Headache and Sleep Reset

A practical, non-emergency plan built around your schedule: **3 x 30-minute workouts/week**, **no caffeine after 2 PM**, and simple daily habits to lower tension headaches and support better sleep.

## Weekly Wellness Plan

| Week | Focus | Exercise (3x/week, 30 min) | Daily Habit | Sleep Goal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Baseline + consistency | Brisk walk, easy bike, light strength | Track headaches, sleep time, triggers | Fixed wake time daily |
| 2 | Posture + movement breaks | Walk + mobility; bodyweight circuit | 2–3 posture breaks during workday | Wind-down starts 45 min before bed |
| 3 | Hydration + regular meals | Moderate cardio + core | Drink steadily through morning/afternoon | Same bedtime 5 nights/week |
| 4 | Stress downshift | Cardio + stretching | 5-minute breathing reset daily | Reduce screen time before bed |
| 5 | Sleep environment | Strength + mobility | Dark, cool, quiet bedroom setup | Bed only for sleep/rest |
| 6 | Headache prevention | Cardio + neck/upper-back mobility | Check jaw/shoulder tension twice daily | Keep sleep/wake times steady |
| 7 | Fine-tune triggers | Mix of cardio and strength | Review food, stress, screen, and hydration patterns | Aim for faster sleep onset |
| 8 | Maintain what works | Favorite 3 workouts | Keep the most effective habits | Lock in a sustainable routine |

## Daily Routine for Headache Relief and Better Sleep

**Morning**
- Get **5–15 minutes of outdoor light** soon after waking.
- Drink a full glass of water.
- Do 2 minutes of neck, shoulder, and upper-back mobility.
- If you use caffeine, keep it earlier in the day and stop by **2 PM**.

**Workday**
- Use a **50/10 or 25/5** focus-break rhythm.
- Every hour, do 30–60 seconds of:
  - shoulder rolls
  - chin tucks
  - chest opener stretch
  - standing and looking far away to relax eye strain
- Keep screens at a comfortable height so your head does not drift forward.
- Eat regular meals; skipped meals can trigger headaches for some people.

**Evening**
- Finish exercise at least **2–3 hours before bed** if possible.
- Dim lights and reduce bright screens in the last **45–60 minutes**.
- Keep the room **cool, dark, and quiet**.
- Use a consistent wind-down: shower, reading, stretching, or calm music.

## Sleep Hygiene Checklist

- [ ] Wake up at the same time every day, including weekends
- [ ] Keep bedtime within about 1 hour most nights
- [ ] No caffeine after 2 PM
- [ ] Limit alcohol near bedtime
- [ ] Avoid large meals right before bed
- [ ] Keep naps short, ideally under 20–30 minutes and not late in the day
- [ ] Use the bed only for sleep and intimacy
- [ ] If you are awake for a long time, get up briefly and do something quiet
- [ ] Turn down lights and screens before bed
- [ ] Keep the bedroom cool and uncluttered

## Hydration, Meals, and Desk-Job Posture

### Hydration
- Aim for steady intake across the day rather than “catching up” at night.
- A simple target for many adults is **pale yellow urine** most of the day.
- Add water around workouts and on dry allergy days.
- If you get headaches from dehydration, keep a bottle at your desk and sip regularly.

### Desk posture
- Feet flat on the floor or on a footrest.
- Hips and knees roughly at 90 degrees.
- Screen top near eye level.
- Elbows near your sides; shoulders relaxed.
- Keyboard and mouse close enough that you do not reach forward.
- If you use a laptop, consider raising it and using an external keyboard/mouse.

### Quick tension-break sequence
- 5 slow shoulder rolls
- 5 chin tucks
- 20-second chest stretch
- 20-second upper-trap stretch each side
- 3 deep breaths with long exhales

## Exercise Plan for 3 Days a Week

**Day A: Cardio + mobility**
- 20 minutes brisk walking, cycling, or elliptical
- 10 minutes mobility: neck, shoulders, thoracic spine, hips

**Day B: Light strength**
- 2–3 rounds of:
  - squats or sit-to-stands
  - wall or incline push-ups
  - rows with band or light weights
  - glute bridges
  - dead bug or bird-dog
- Keep effort moderate, not exhausting

**Day C: Cardio + relaxation**
- 20 minutes moderate cardio
- 10 minutes stretching or yoga-style recovery

## When to See a Clinician

Make an appointment if any of these happen:
- Headaches become **more frequent, more severe, or change in pattern**
- Headaches wake you from sleep or are consistently worse in the morning
- You develop **vision changes, weakness, numbness, confusion, fainting, fever, or neck stiffness**
- Headaches start after a head injury
- Over-the-counter pain relief is needed often, or headaches persist despite good sleep and hydration
- Sleep problems last **more than 8 weeks** or cause major daytime impairment
- Loud snoring, gasping, or witnessed breathing pauses suggest possible sleep apnea
- Allergy symptoms are persistent enough to disrupt sleep, especially with congestion or mouth breathing

## Quick Actions
